{{distinguish|text=the [[splitting lemma]] in [[homological algebra]]}}

In [[mathematics]], especially in [[singularity theory]], the '''splitting lemma''' is a useful result due to [[René Thom]] which provides a way of simplifying the local expression of a [[function (mathematics)|function]] usually applied in a [[neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhood]] of a degenerate [[critical point (mathematics)|critical point]]. 

==Formal statement==
Let <math>f:(\mathbb{R}^n, 0) \to (\mathbb{R}, 0)</math> be a smooth function germ, with a critical point at 0 (so <math>(\partial f/\partial x_i)(0) = 0</math> for <math>i = 1, \dots, n</math>). Let ''V'' be a [[linear subspace|subspace]] of <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> such that the [[restriction (mathematics)|restriction]] ''f''&thinsp;|<sub>''V''</sub> is [[critical point (mathematics)|non-degenerate]], and write ''B'' for the [[Hessian matrix]] of this restriction.  Let ''W'' be any complementary subspace to ''V''.  Then there is a change of coordinates <math>\Phi(x, y)</math> of the form <math>\Phi(x, y) = (\phi(x, y), y)</math> with <math>x \in V, y \in W</math>, and a smooth function ''h'' on ''W'' such that
:<math>f\circ\Phi(x,y) = \frac{1}{2} x^TBx + h(y).</math>

This result is often referred to as the parametrized [[Morse lemma]], which can be seen by viewing ''y'' as the parameter. It is the ''gradient version'' of the [[implicit function theorem]].

==Extensions==
There are extensions to infinite dimensions, to [[complex analytic function]]s, to functions invariant under the [[group action|action]] of a [[compact group]], ...
